producer_report.summary: An exempt commit now also excuses the job records it adds. `jobs::check` returns early for a commit on the `[history] exempt` list, as `invariant::check` already did. Both checks use one new helper, `invariant::is_exempt`. It uses the tip's list in a history walk and the parent's list in a per-commit check. Two new tests in `history.rs` cover the behaviour: an exempt commit's hand-written landed outcome and score.json are not flagged, while the same records in a non-exempt commit, or in a commit after the exempt one, are. I added decision D68 (citing D66/D67) and a CHANGELOG line. All three checks pass: `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`.

checks_run.note: 6 exemption tests pass, including the 2 new ones
applied formatting; I did not run `--check` afterwards

open_issues: I did not run the history check against the real repository, so I have not confirmed the 9 violations for the six jobs disappear there. The new tests reproduce the same two violation kinds on a synthetic history.
D68 says it corrects D67's claim that the exempt commit's jobs 'still get the per-record checks', but D67 itself is unchanged.
Out of scope and untouched: confirming ee4b0dd is in main's history, and the exempt list in athena.toml.
mistakes: My first draft of the test records used null `totals`, which the record validator rejects, so the non-exempt test failed. I fixed it by building the outcome with real Quantity values through serde_json.
I tried to append D68 with a shell here-document, which the policy denied. I used the Edit tool instead.
learnings: `jobs::check` parses an outcome only if it is a valid record. A request job's outcome needs non-null `totals`, so a hand-written landed outcome with null totals is reported as ValidRecords and never reaches the JobRecords check.
Without the early return, a hand-written score.json is flagged 'does not follow' and a landed outcome is flagged 'not a valid landing'. The new non-exempt test asserts both messages.

The history check's tip-level ValidRecords and reconcile passes still run on an exempt commit's records. The exemption only skips the per-commit checks. The new test's records are valid and reconcile, so it passes.
`crates/athena-gate/tests/policy.rs` (the enforcement-map test) still passes after I added tests, so no map entry was needed for them.
desires: The real `athena check --history` output for main, to confirm the six jobs clear.
A `tail` or output-limiting option on cargo commands, since long cargo output cannot be trimmed.
